title: LLM-Based Weak Annotation for Cybersecurity Tweet Classification: A Teacher-Student Framework
abstract: arXiv:2610.21254v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) relies on the timely identification of emerging threats, enabling organizations and security analysts to support situational awareness and decision-making. Social media platforms such as X (formerly Twitter) have become valuable CTI sources because vulnerabilities and attack activities are often discussed there before appearing in formal reports. However, the rapid growth of cybersecurity discussions on social media has created more content than domain experts can realistically review and annotate, making labeled data a major bottleneck for developing supervised learning approaches. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as weak annotators in other domains, their effectiveness for cybersecurity tweet classification and downstream training of domain-specific pre-trained language models (PLMs) remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose a Teacher-Student weak supervision frame

translated_title: 基于大语言模型的网络安全推文分类弱标注：一种师生框架
translated_abstract: 网络威胁情报（CTI）依赖于对新兴威胁的及时识别，从而帮助组织和安全分析师支持态势感知与决策制定。像X（前身为Twitter）这样的社交媒体平台已成为宝贵的CTI来源，因为漏洞和攻击活动通常在出现在正式报告之前就会在这些平台上被讨论。然而，社交媒体上网络安全讨论的快速增长产生了超出领域专家实际可审查和标注范围的内容，使得标注数据成为开发监督学习方法的主要瓶颈。尽管大语言模型（LLM）在其他领域作为弱标注器已展现出潜力，但其在网络安全推文分类以及领域特定预训练语言模型（PLM）下游训练中的有效性仍未得到充分探索。为应对这一挑战，我们提出了一种师生弱监督框架……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个以大语言模型作为弱标注器的师生弱监督框架，旨在解决网络安全推文分类中专家标注数据稀缺的瓶颈问题，并有效支持领域特定预训练语言模型的下游训练。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Teacher-Student weak supervision framework that leverages LLMs as weak annotators to address the labeled data bottleneck in cybersecurity tweet classification and enable effective downstream training of domain-specific pre-trained language models.
